scope: REQUIREMENTS.md Part A §10-13: pi-review round cap and stall watchdog, pi-worker, skills contract, the repo test runner (packages/nana-pack, scripts/test.mjs) — 24 off-form origins
notes:
ASTRA R1 FIX ROUND (BLOCK 5/10 -> this revision). astra r1's key finding, applied throughout: 'a recorded red mutation proves sensitivity to that mutation; it does not establish coverage of every condition or outcome in the row' — so every implemented clause below was re-checked by mutating EACH condition/outcome its own text names, not just the one mutation that happened to work. MUST 1 (reject all three merges): R-711, R-718 and R-727 are now split, each confirmed by an EXECUTED counterexample that leaves one promise green while the other reds (not just asserted): R-711 — mtime-in-dirty-hash breaks 'revert the edit' while 're-reviewing an already-counted revision' and 'worktree W2...' stay green (both clean-commit scenarios, untouched by a dirty-hash mutation); R-718 — forcing `mine=false` breaks only 'complete(B) recorded...' (own-a-live-reservation) while the three invalid-reservation refusals are already correct regardless; R-727 — wrong exit code (0) breaks only the status half of the one cited test while 'running the watchdog first' (astra's own technique) breaks only its never-runs half, confirming the merge hid two independently-breakable facts. MUST 2 (restore the directory-lock-path refusal): new R-852 restores 'a directory lock path shall be refused at once with a message and no stack, before the review runs' as its own row (R-723 stays the general 'every ledger path shall be a regular file'; R-844 is reworded to drop the unproven 'at once' for the symlink/unwritable-directory cases specifically, since astra's 4-second-delay counterexample showed neither of those two citations checks timing). MUST 3 (six PARTIAL rows): R-833 downgraded to untested (no assertion pins preservation of the literal --revision value, only acceptance); R-843 split so 'naming file and line' is claimed only for the malformed/corrupted case (the only one the citation proves), with incomplete-record refusal split into its own row, R-853, without that unproven guarantee; R-844 — see MUST 2; R-846 downgraded to untested (its only citation launches pi-worker, a neighbouring case, not pi-review); R-910 gains a second, dual-tagged citation (the existing non-zero-exit assertion) plus its own new mutation, since the original citation covered only the exit-0-plus-FAIL-line half; R-912 narrowed to the timeout trigger only (dual-citing R-609's own process-tree-kill evidence), with the Ctrl-C/SIGTERM trigger split into new R-915, untested — astra's counterexample (clearing active/ scratch at the top of the signal handler) leaves the entire 24-check file green, confirming no test sends a signal to the runner. SHOULD (standalone sentences): R-842, R-845, R-846, R-847, R-849, R-911, R-912, R-913, R-914 reworded to name their own subject/condition instead of a sibling-dependent pronoun or elliptical opener. NOTE correction (round 1 claim, since superseded — see ASTRA R2 FIX ROUND below: R-831 is now untested, so it carries no mutation at all; this round-1 paragraph is kept for history only): the round-1 fix intended to replace R-831's recorded mutation with importing `canonicalItem` from review-round.mjs instead of re-importing `reviewShaped`, to isolate the import promise cleanly, but astra r2 found the JSON's actual `break` text was never updated to match — a real discrepancy, now moot since R-831 has no mutation to misdescribe. R-911's mutation is corrected per astra's NOTE: the original (`f === 0` added to `ok`) also suppressed the WARN push (`if (ok && f)` requires `ok`), so it did not isolate 'shall not flip the verdict' from R-606's 'reported as a WARN'; the new mutation touches only the LABEL computation, confirmed to leave the WARN line intact. Isolated-reproduction scripts for R-723/R-852, R-837 and R-721 (plus one for R-718, not explicitly requested but written on the same ground: forcing `mine=false` to isolate 'own a live reservation' is too destructive to run against the full file) are committed at docs/reviews/ears-form-2026-10-04/isolated-repro-{r723,r837,r721,r718}.mjs, each run standalone at both baseline (PASS) and under its mutation (FAIL) before being recorded here. R-723/R-852's script carries NO added timeout — astra r1 SHOULD corrected this worker's earlier, wrong claim that the cited call hangs forever; it fails correctly via ledgerRun's own existing 30000ms spawnSync timeout, confirmed at ~31s against the REAL file (not a substitute) before the isolated script was written for fast iteration. R-721's script keeps both conjuncts of the real assertion (absence of .1 AND three retained rounds), not just the first. R-837's script discloses its one necessary adaptation (guarding the cleanup unlink so the script itself can still report a result when the mutation has already removed the lock). Sibling-cite list (round 1, 6 entries — superseded, see ASTRA R2 FIX ROUND below for the current list of 2): R-831, R-852, R-854 and R-851 are mostly moot now that R-831, R-852, R-727 and R-851 are untested (R-854 still nominally 'shares' R-727's cites field, since downgrading left that field in place on the origin for context even though its status no longer makes evidentiary use of it); R-911 and R-914 remain as legitimate two-different-mutations siblings (R-914 also now untested, so only R-911/R-606 remains live).

ASTRA R2 FIX ROUND (BLOCK 6/10, Fable's read-and-replay shape, bc-method-ruling.md §4 -> this revision). No round 3; this is a mechanical downgrade pass, not a new mutation hunt.
Form MUSTs: (1) R-851's condition restored — 'WHEN pi-review receives --worker, the review shall never run.' — and R-854 reworded to name pi-review explicitly ('A pi-review invocation carrying --worker shall be refused.'). Both R-727 and R-851 are ALSO downgraded to untested this round per the gap audit below (the brief: 'do not try to rescue rows with new mutations this round' — the condition fix is a text/honesty correction, not a rescue, and the downgrade applies regardless). R-854 stays implemented (clean per astra r2's own 46-row read) and keeps the marker alone. (2) R-844's 'at once' restored for the symlink and unwritable-directory cases ('A symlink or an unwritable ledger directory shall be refused AT ONCE with a message and no stack, before the review runs.') — astra r2's own read found the row under-covered well beyond just 'at once' (only the unwritable-directory message is mutated; timing, no-stack, before-review-runs and the whole symlink case are not), so R-844 is also downgraded to untested wholesale this round, honestly carrying the full restored promise rather than a trimmed one. (3) R-853's 'naming file and line' guarantee for the incomplete-tally-line case is restored as its own new row, R-855, untested (R-853 itself is unchanged and stays implemented — clean per astra r2 — since its narrower text, without the diagnostic claim, is exactly what its citation proves).
Status gaps (astra r2 §2, 27 rows, 58.7% of 46 implemented clauses): every row astra's gap table named is downgraded to untested here — R-702, R-831, R-703, R-706, R-834, R-850, R-715, R-838, R-718, R-839, R-719, R-720, R-842, R-843, R-723, R-852, R-844, R-725, R-845, R-727, R-851, R-728, R-847, R-605, R-913, R-615, R-914 — each with an explicit `evidence` string naming astra's own 'uncovered words' and record-limitation text verbatim, so the cell doubles as the 6b coverage-completion worklist. No new mutation was recorded for any of these 27 this round (per the brief: gaps are listed, not gated; the seat downgrades and lands). Every `// req:` marker previously assigned to one of these 27 rows alone is removed; markers still shared with a row that STAYS implemented (R-910, R-606, R-911, R-609, R-912, R-722, R-735, R-854, R-717, R-612, R-729) are kept, trimmed to just the surviving id(s). Record-description discrepancies (item 3 of the brief): R-831's `break` text was never actually updated to the round-1-intended `canonicalItem` import (astra r2 caught this as a real mismatch between the notes' claim and the mapping) — moot now, since R-831 has no mutation at all post-downgrade; the round-1 notes paragraph above is marked superseded rather than silently deleted. R-852's `break` text overclaimed that all four of the cited assertion's ANDed conditions flip under the mutation; astra r2's replay showed the timeout produces empty stderr, so `noStack()` remains true (only status and elapsed-time flip) — corrected in R-852's own `evidence` string above (R-852 is also now untested, folded into the 27-row gap list). The 19 rows astra's round-2 audit found clean stay implemented, unchanged: R-707, R-710, R-835, R-836, R-711, R-837, R-717, R-840, R-841, R-721, R-853, R-854, R-735, R-910, R-606, R-911, R-609, R-912, R-613.
